question: Serbia Parliamentary Election Winner
resolution_criteria:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

"Other" means any option not listed here.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-11: The Republic Electoral Commission (RIK, rik.parlament.gov.rs) has not yet published any results, because the vote is on 2026-10-25. I could not fetch a live status from the RIK site. Lists appear on the ballot in the order RIK proclaimed them, not by lottery. [N1 (rule as described in 2023)](https://n1info.rs/english/news/the-lists-on-the-ballot-for-the-early-parliamentary-elections/)
- Mid-September 2026: RIK proclaimed the Student List, which is third on the ballot. RIK also proclaimed "Russian Party - Slobodan Nikolić" and other lists. [021.rs](https://www.021.rs/info/srbija/359721/rik-proglasio-izborne-liste-cedomira-jovanovica-i-ruske-stranke), [N1](https://n1info.rs/vesti/rik-proglasio-listu-cale-ovo-je-za-tebe/)
- I found no single source with the complete ballot order.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. As of 2026-10-11 it is a two-way contest between "Aleksandar Vučić - United Serbia" (led by SNS, Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party) and "Student List - Students Win". No other list polls anywhere near first place.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- October 2026: Jacobin reports the Student List campaigning under the slogan "Serbia or Mafia", focused on corruption. Most opposition parties stood aside to give it a clear run. [Jacobin](https://jacobin.com/2026/10/elections-serbia-student-list-vucic)
- 2026-09-14 (approx.): The Student List was submitted to RIK, headed by Ilija Srdanović. United Serbia has named Vučić as its candidate for prime minister. The Student List has named none. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Serbian_parliamentary_election)
- 2026-09-09: Vučić dissolved parliament and called a snap election for 2026-10-25. The vote was not due until 2027. It comes after nearly two years of anti-government protests, and Vučić is seeking to become prime minister. [Cyprus Mail/Reuters](https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/09/09/serbias-president-vucic-dissolves-parliament-calls-snap-elections), [Ahram](https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/576333.aspx)
- 2026-09-07: The government, under PM Đuro Macut, proposed the dissolution. [Internazionale/Reuters](https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-notizie-reuters/2026/09/07/serbia-s-government-to-propose-dissolving-parliament-for-an-election-report-says)

## 4. Base rates and polls
- History: an SNS-led list has come first in every parliamentary election since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023). This is from my background knowledge, with 2022 confirmed by [Tanjug](https://www.tanjug.rs/english/politics/65380/serbia-must-not-stop-list-won-4664-pct-of-votes-commission/vest).
- Polls published on or before 2026-10-11 (decided voters): [Wikipedia polling page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Serbian_parliamentary_election)

| Pollster | Published | SNS list | Student List | SPS (Dačić) | Lead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Faktor Plus | 2026-09-21 | 48.6% | 37.1% | 4.9% | SNS +11.5 |
| Faktor Plus | 2026-09-04 | 47.2% | 31.5% | 4.9% | SNS +15.7 |
| NSPM | 2026-07-30 | 37.5% | 39.6% | 4.9% | Students +2.1 |
| CRTA | 2026-07-15 | 35.7% | 44.9% | n/a | Students +9.2 |
| Faktor Plus | 2026-06-26 | 47.1% | 30.7% | 5.0% | SNS +16.4 |
| Faktor Plus | 2026-04-30 | 46.4% | 28.7% | n/a | SNS +17.7 (page states +19.7) |

- 2026-07-15: CRTA's poll was the first regular national poll since July 2010 to put anyone other than SNS in first place. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Serbian_parliamentary_election)
- The pollsters split along political lines. Faktor Plus (often seen as government-leaning) consistently shows SNS ahead by double digits. CRTA and NSPM (independent or opposition-leaning) show the Student List ahead.
- The trend in Faktor Plus is the Student List closing the gap, from 17.7 points behind in April to 11.5 behind in September.
- Smaller lists are well short of first place. Dačić's SPS list polls around 3 to 5%, and minority lists (Hungarian, Bosniak, Ljajić) usually win a handful of seats each.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not get Polymarket odds: the page is blocked for US visitors and showed no prices. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/serbia-parliamentary-election-winner)
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold markets and no published expert seat forecasts dated before 2026-10-11.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More pre-election polls are likely in the final two weeks, from NSPM, Ipsos, Faktor Plus and CRTA.
- Campaign incidents, plus concerns about the integrity of the vote (pressure on voters, vote-buying, the voter roll), which NGOs have historically raised in Serbian elections.
- 2026-10-25: election day. CeSID and Ipsos usually publish projections on the night, and RIK releases preliminary results within about a day.
- Seats are allocated by proportional representation (the D'Hondt method) with a 3% threshold. Minority lists are exempt from the threshold. So a list that wins the popular vote will almost certainly also win the most seats.
